See relationship risk before outreach becomes reactive

Unify sentiment, complaints, engagement, and product context into a transparent review queue with human-controlled retention options and no automated customer action.

**Why try it:** A relationship manager can ask who needs attention, see the exact synthetic signals behind the priority, and prepare outreach options without treating a score as a fact.

## Problem Statement

A regional bank has customer feedback, complaints, surveys, and engagement signals spread across channels. Teams react late and may apply generic offers without a clear evidence trail or review control.

## Solution Summary

Microsoft Copilot Studio gives relationship teams a governed conversational view. Dynamics 365 supplies customer-service context, approved interaction analytics contribute signals, Power BI shows segment trends, and Microsoft Teams supports outreach review.

**Blueprint role:** Creates a governed relationship-intelligence layer connecting customer signals, transparent prioritization, service recovery, and approved outreach.

**Capabilities:** Cross-channel sentiment view; Churn-review prioritization; Retention option preparation; Segment context. See [responsibilities and trust boundaries](2.Architecture.md).

## Business Outcomes

- Improves visibility into cross-channel experience signals.
- Makes churn prioritization explainable rather than presenting a hidden prediction as fact.
- Keeps outreach, offers, fee changes, and account actions under authorized human control.

Claims are qualitative; synthetic demo figures are not customer results or performance commitments. See the [claims policy](../../solutions/README.md#claims-policy).

## Target Users

| Role | Need |
| --- | --- |
| Relationship Managers | Prepare reviewable retention options before anyone contacts a customer or changes a fee. |
| Retention Specialists | See who to review first and the synthetic evidence behind each heuristic priority. |
| Customer Success Teams | Review cross-channel sentiment and segment context to decide which relationship needs attention. |

## In Scope / Out of Scope

### In scope

- Aggregate fictional interaction sentiment, NPS, products and complaints across touchpoints.
- Rank customers for human review with a disclosed weighted heuristic, never as an individual prediction.
- Prepare service-recovery and outreach options for review without contacting anyone or making offers.
- Compare synthetic segment NPS and product averages with fixed benchmarks to guide investigation.

### Out of scope / approval boundary

- No browsing or live voice, chat, survey, complaint, CRM, account or product data, and no unstated personal information.
- No customer contact, outreach, case or task creation, CRM or account change, or segment change.
- No fee waivers or changes, compensation, offers or transactions.
- No legal, regulatory, insurance, lending, tax, investment or financial advice, and no sensitive-circumstance inference.
- No claim that a customer will or will not churn.
- No workshop publishing: the validated manual and pilot agents stay Draft with `published: false`.

## Qualification Checklist

- [ ] Is a Copilot Studio target environment available, and can the Easy-mode team run PAC CLI 2.9.3 or newer?
- [ ] Has the customer mapped customer-service context, interaction analytics, segment reporting and outreach review to approved systems?
- [ ] Are organization-specific privacy, fairness, suitability, retention, legal, compliance and financial controls defined?
- [ ] Will the customer own and validate the prioritization heuristic, its thresholds and weights before use?
- [ ] Are authorized Relationship Managers, Retention Specialists or Customer Success Leads named to review every priority and option?
- [ ] Will connections be least-privilege, with consequential actions behind explicit approval and publication approved separately?
- [ ] Have governance, telemetry, support and success measures been agreed before production?

## What Actually Goes Wrong

- **indicator-drift:** The indicator reference lists a stale-survey factor the score never applies and describes a segment-average transaction test that the code runs against a fixed threshold.
- **oldest-sentiment-shown:** The high-risk recent-sentiment line reads the last listed interaction, which is the oldest when records are ordered newest first.
- **score-as-prediction:** A heuristic priority score is presented as a prediction that a customer will churn.
- **unapproved-retention-action:** A retention option is carried out as outreach, a fee waiver or an offer without approval.
- **illustrative-economics:** Illustrative action costs and success rates are treated as expected outcomes.
- **sensitive-inference:** Feedback signals are used to infer sensitive circumstances or to give financial advice.

See [state and recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery).
